details: Plogme is a WhatsApp/Baileys protocol fork that pulls malicious code into the install tree and covertly annotates the user's outgoing messages. Three behaviours verified in the published files: 1. Dependency on a malicious release. package.json declares "cache-manager": "^7.2.8", which resolves to cache-manager@7.2.10, a release distributed as malicious. lib/Store/make-cache-manager-store.js imports createCache from it to back the WhatsApp auth state, so the malicious module is loaded on a normal install. 2. Hidden third-party channel annotation on every upload. lib/Utils/channel-policy.js exports getMediaChannelAnnotations(), which returns ContextInfo.ForwardedNewsletterMessageInfo metadata pointing at newsletter JID 120363402922206865@newsletter, display name "crysnovax", contentType UPDATE, and serverMessageId built from hex "313033" ("103"). lib/Utils/messages.js imports and attaches this to every outgoing image and video message, so each upload carries channel-promotion metadata the installer never asked for and cannot see. A comment in the file claims the metadata "does not follow, subscribe to, or otherwise modify newsletter subscriptions", which understates what it does. 3. Embedded WhatsApp service credentials and a third-party version endpoint. lib/Defaults/ban-checker.js hardcodes a WhatsApp GraphQL access token and doc id used by lib/Socket/ban-checker.js to POST ban-appeal status queries to hxxps://graph[.]whatsapp[.]com/graphql. lib/Utils/generics.js fetches the protocol version from the third-party host hxxps://pair[.]crysnovax[.]link instead of WhatsApp, and that host is also embedded as a sticker-pack publisher credit in lib/Utils/messages.js. The preinstall hook engine-requirements.js only reads process.versions.node and exits when the Node major version is below 20. No access to.npmrc, NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH keys or other installer credential files was found in the package.
